build_spec.authority: Complete resolved typed build contract. Defined behavior is mandatory; explicitly unspecified cases remain unspecified. Frozen implementation identities do not turn incidental values in unspecified cases into requirements.

modules.behavior: Combinational CORDIC quadrant pre-rotation. Formats (all two's complement, ports unsigned bit vectors): angle is a 16-bit binary angle, theta = angle * 2*pi / 2^16 radians (one turn = 2^16); x and y are 18-bit Q2.16 (value / 2^16); z and atan values are 20-bit in units of 2^-20 turn; cos_out and sin_out are 16-bit Q2.14 (value / 2^14). K = 39797 = round(2^16 * prod_{i=0..15} 1/sqrt(1 + 2^-2i)). Quadrant q = angle[15:14]. When q is 01 or 10 (|theta| >= pi/2) the start vector is rotated by half a turn: x0 = -K (2^18 - 39797) and the reduced angle is angle ^ 0x8000; otherwise x0 = K and the reduced angle is angle. z0 = sign-extended reduced angle * 16, i.e. {reduced[15:0], 4'b0000}, a 20-bit value in 2^-20 turns within [-2^18, 2^18). The start vector's y is 0 (not a port). Python oracle: combinational and stateless; step returns the outputs for this step's inputs (latency 0, no clock and no reset port).
modules.name: cordic_prerot

modules.behavior: Combinational CORDIC arctangent table: atan = round(atan(2^-idx) / (2*pi) * 2^20), round half up, in 2^-20 turn units, for idx 0..15: 131072, 77376, 40884, 20753, 10417, 5213, 2607, 1304, 652, 326, 163, 81, 41, 20, 10, 5. Python oracle: combinational and stateless; step returns the outputs for this step's inputs (latency 0, no clock and no reset port).
modules.name: cordic_atan

modules.behavior: Iterative CORDIC rotation engine, one micro-rotation per rising edge, 16 iterations, with valid/ready-style handshake ports carried as plain protocol none signals. Formats (all two's complement, ports unsigned bit vectors): angle is a 16-bit binary angle, theta = angle * 2*pi / 2^16 radians (one turn = 2^16); x and y are 18-bit Q2.16 (value / 2^16); z and atan values are 20-bit in units of 2^-20 turn; cos_out and sin_out are 16-bit Q2.14 (value / 2^14). Registers, all reset to 0: busy, out_valid, i[3:0], x[17:0], y[17:0], z[19:0]. Outputs, all views of registered state: in_ready = !busy && !out_valid; out_valid; iter = i; x; y. atan_val is the table value for index iter (from the atan table neighbour); x0 and z0 come from the pre-rotation of the input angle. At each rising edge with rst low, using pre-edge values: if busy: with xs = x >>> i and ys = y >>> i (arithmetic shifts of the 18-bit two's complement values, rounding toward minus infinity), if z >= 0 (z[19] = 0) then x = x - ys, y = y + xs, z = z - atan_val, else x = x + ys, y = y - xs, z = z + atan_val (x and y modulo 2^18, z modulo 2^20); i = i + 1 modulo 16; and when i was 15, busy = 0 and out_valid = 1. Else if out_valid: out_valid = 0 when out_ready = 1 (x and y hold). Else (idle) if in_valid = 1: accept: x = x0, y = 0, z = z0, i = 0, busy = 1. in_valid, x0 and z0 are ignored except at the accepting edge. An accepted angle takes 16 busy edges and out_valid appears after the 16th; the next angle can be accepted at the edge after the output transfer at the earliest. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge returns every register to its reset value; reset has no effect between edges. Python oracle: cycle-level model, one step per rising edge; keep the registers in state and return every output as it is after that edge. The driver applies the fixed latency of 1; do not add a delay queue. init() is the reset state and a supplied rst must be handled.
modules.name: cordic_engine

modules.behavior: Combinational CORDIC output stage: Q2.16 to Q2.14 with round half up. cos_out = ((x_in + 2) >>> 2) and sin_out = ((y_in + 2) >>> 2), where x_in and y_in are 18-bit two's complement, the sum is formed without overflow (19 bits) and the result is its low 16 bits (bits [17:2] of the 19-bit sum, wrapping for out-of-range inputs that the engine never produces). Python oracle: combinational and stateless; step returns the outputs for this step's inputs (latency 0, no clock and no reset port).
modules.name: cordic_out

declared_latency.meaning: A source annotation declares numeric latency only when present. This known/cycles pair is authoritative for the current top module's annotation requirement. Only known=true requires a matching numeric top annotation. Child typed-module latency does not invent a top annotation for arbitrary aggregate wrappers. When known=false, absence of a top annotation is not a failed or unverifiable criterion. Unannotated numeric latency is UNKNOWN, not zero. Preserve the source's exact observable cycles and registered behavior. Annotation presence or absence alone is not independent proof of behavioral correctness; use the fixed source contract, all defined typed latency/minimum transfer age and deterministic verification, without inventing a numeric requirement.

implementation.meaning: Chip-top implementation: the top is the whole FPGA design. Every port bit gets an I/O buffer on a package pin, and data ports have zero input and output delay to clk, so the routed WNS and WHS include pad delay. Utilization includes the I/O buffers.

metric_provenance: Structured metrics are parsed from retained reports; routed utilization/timing reports take precedence when present. The manifest identifies complete files by hash. Header excerpts are bounded previews, not complete reports or an independent metric source.
objective_policy: First establish timing feasibility. A verified timing-feasible candidate may replace a known timing-infeasible previous best even with higher area or power; classify this as timing_recovery, not objective savings. While the previous best is timing-infeasible, a verified still-infeasible candidate with strictly better setup WNS and hold not worse beyond a small tolerance may replace it as timing_progress, which is not closure; a feasible candidate always outranks it. Once both are timing-feasible, require strict improvement of the chosen objective; for maximize_freq that is register-to-register setup slack (reg2reg_wns_ns) when both designs report it, otherwise full setup WNS for both, while feasibility stays on full WNS and WHS. minimize_luts compares (lut_used, ff_used) and minimize_ffs compares (ff_used, lut_used) lexicographically: an equal primary metric with a strictly lower secondary is an objective improvement, a higher primary never is, and a secondary missing from either design gives no tie-break. Unknown or contradictory incumbent timing evidence cannot establish recovery. A completed experiment may find no improvement. Do not invent mandatory savings, slack margins, tool versions, timing corners, new tests, thresholds, code-style quotas or external environment requirements.
